purpose: Measure prospective generalization of the canonical 1,001-concept English architecture without vocabulary tuning against the test.
evidence_sequence: Freeze explicit held-out battery in a commit containing no score.
Record exact battery commit and blob identity.
Only after freeze, reconstruct the canonical 1,001 set from authority files.
Score every frozen task under the predeclared A/B/C law.
Write the result without modifying the battery.
Verify battery blob is unchanged from freeze commit and canonical vocabulary authorities are unchanged.

scoring_classes.A: All direct lexical requirements needed for the task are available under the canonical lexical authority plus productive grammar, morphology, and numeration.
scoring_classes.B: The direct compressed label is unavailable, but at least one predeclared controlled-paraphrase path is fully constructible and preserves the task-relevant proposition.
scoring_classes.C: Neither direct expression nor an authorized semantically adequate paraphrase path is available.

safety_law: For safety-critical medical, emergency, legal, financial, identity, or hazard tasks, a paraphrase is creditable only when the frozen task explicitly supplies an equivalence-preserving path. Broader or merely related language does not count.
interpretation_law: This is a prospective internally generated held-out benchmark, stronger than the prior aggregate-constrained reconstruction because the task records are frozen before scoring.
It is not an independent third-party human trial or external standardized assessment.
A high result supports generalization across this new battery but does not prove complete coverage of all English communication.
